newsitem.title: GERMANY: Austria on way to qualifying for EMU - Liebscher.
newsitem.headline: Austria on way to qualifying for EMU - Liebscher.

text.p: Austria is well on the way to qualifying for European monetary union and does not want the start to be delayed or entry criteria to be softened, National Bank President Klaus Liebscher said on Monday.
Discussion of timing or criteria would be "inappropriate", Liebscher said in extracts released from a speech he was due to make in the evening to Bavarian bankers.

Austria, which has for long pegged its schilling currency to the German mark, is widely regarded as one of the "core" European Union member states likely to take part in the launch of the Euro currency, which is scheduled for 1999.
Liebscher said Austria already met the Maastricht treaty's terms covering inflation and interest rates.
The Austrian government has adopted a budget consolidation programme which will ensure Maastricht's budget deficit ceiling of three percent of gross domestic product is met.
And, Liebscher added, steps are being taken to ensure that Austria's national debt is reduced to meet the 60 percent goal stipulated in the treaty.
